description.narrative: Construction of Makambako-Songea transmission line and distribution lines to provide sustained access to reliable and affordable electricity within six districts in the Iringa and Ruvuma regions of Southern Tanzania (Ref 71002060 credit part)

Konstruktion av Makambako-Songea transmission och distributions-linjer för tillgång till hållbar, tillförlig elektricitet till överkomligt pris inom sex distrikt i regionerna Iringa och Ruvuma i södra Tanzania.

The major objective of the project was to extend TANESCOs electricity network in order to provide electricity to commercial business activities, fresh water pumping, secondary schools, medical services, streetlights, residential houses, etc. within the project area. The project aimed to provide and improve supply of electricity to economic centers, social and welfare utilities and households in rural villages, peri-urban areas and towns in Njombe and Ruvuma regions in Tanzania.

sector.narrative: Electric power transmission and distribution (centralised grids)

description.narrative:
The project has had a long gestation period, from the initial feasibility study conducted in 2006 up to its completion in June 2025. Nevertheless, all transmission lines and substations were completed and energised in September 2018. All distribution networks were finalised in June 2025, at which point the project target of 23,232 electricity connections was fully achieved.
During the reporting period July 2020June 2021, TANESCO submitted the Final Project Implementation Report to the Embassy of Sweden. In January 2025, TANESCO further submitted a report confirming the completion of the final 2,607 customer connections. These two reports, together with field observations and experience from the Programme Officer, form the basis for this performance monitoring, the assessment of project results, and the preparation of this project completion memo.
Overall, the reports provide a comprehensive overview of the activities implemented and the achievements attained. They also identify several challenges encountered during project implementation, which are important to note for all parties involved, including the Embassy, the Ministry of Energy (MoE), the Ministry of Finance (MoF), TANESCO, and REA. A summary of achieved results both expected and unexpectedis presented below.
Transmission Sub-Project: The Transmission Sub-Project comprised the construction of 245 km of 220 kV overhead transmission line from Makambako to Songea, the extension of the Makambako 220/132/33 kV substation, and the construction of new Madaba and Songea 220/33 kV substations. The project also included the installation of an Optical Ground Wire (OPGW) for communication purposes, which has been completed and is fully operational.
Distribution Sub-Project: The Distribution Sub-Project consisted of consultancy services and the construction of 932 km of 33 kV distribution lines, installation of 282 units of 33 kV/400 V transformers, development of low-voltage distribution networks, and electricity connections to approximately 23,232 customers in 120 villages across the districts of Njombe, Ludewa, Songea, Namtumbo, and Mbinga in Njombe and Ruvuma regions.
Environmental Achievements: As a result of energising the new transmission lines from the national grid and connecting areas previously supplied by diesel-powered generators, substantial reductions in carbon dioxide (CO) emissions have been achieved. Additional environmental benefits include reduced fuel transportation and lower risks of fuel spills and contamination. Total CO savings up to June 2020 are estimated at 28,630 tonnes.
Benefits for the Population: The expected outputs and objectives of the project have largely been achieved. The expansion of the electricity network through the construction of approximately 930 km of 33 kV distribution lines and 680 km of low-voltage networks, and the connection of 23,232 new customers has significantly improved the quality of life for the connected population.
The electrification of schools, clinics, religious institutions, and government buildings has enabled more reliable and sustainable access to electricity, resulting in tangible social benefits. For example, electric lighting has increased study time and improved learning environments for both boys and girls, while health facilities can now operate more effectively during night-time hours.
In combination with the installation of street lighting, which has enhanced security during dark hours, and the reduced reliance on unhealthy kerosene lamps, the project has contributed to improved health and safety conditions.
Overall, the electrification project has contributed to poverty reduction by increasing labour opportunities for both men and women, raising household per capita income, and improving educational outcomes for children. More than 100,000 people living in 23,232 households across 120 villages are identified as beneficiaries of the new transmission and distribution infrastructure.
Additional Economic and Environmental Benefits: Beyond electrification, the project has enabled TANESCO to decommission diesel power stations in Songea, Mbinga, Namtumbo, and Ludewa. This has resulted in cost savings for the Government and the elimination of air pollution associated with diesel generation and fuel transportation from Dar es Salaam. The project therefore represents a significant step towards a cleaner energy sector, contributing to reduced greenhouse gas emissions and a healthier environment.
Furthermore, local businesses have emerged in several newly connected villages. Access to reliable electricity has enabled extended business operating hours and created employment opportunities, generating additional income for surrounding communities and supporting local economic development.
